restatements.text: Carrying a concealed handgun requires a permit from the county sheriff.
The sheriff must issue a permit to anyone who is 21 or older, legally allowed to have a handgun, and has finished an eight-hour safety course.

evidence.quote: No person may carry a concealed handgun without a concealed carry permit issued by the county sheriff.
evidence.why: It bans carrying a concealed handgun without first obtaining a permit.
It adds an eight-hour training requirement to legally carry a concealed handgun.

evidence.quote: concealed carry permit issued by the county sheriff.
evidence.why: It creates a new permit mandate administered by the county sheriff.

evidence.quote: No person may carry a concealed handgun without a concealed carry permit issued by the county sheriff.
evidence.why: It restricts the legal ability to carry a concealed handgun by requiring a permit.
It limits the ability to carry a concealed handgun to those who complete an eight-hour training.

evidence.quote: concealed carry permit issued by the county sheriff.
evidence.why: It expands regulatory powers by requiring individuals to obtain a permit from the county sheriff.

analysis.answer: Current law allows permitless concealed carry for those 21 and older who can lawfully possess a handgun. The proposed measure removes permitless carry and requires obtaining a permit issued by the county sheriff.

It addresses the perceived risk of untrained individuals carrying concealed firearms by imposing a formal permitting process. This creates a time and financial entry barrier to carrying a concealed handgun.

The effect of concealed carry permitting requirements on public safety and crime rates is empirically disputed. Some researchers find that stricter permitting regimes reduce violent crime and accidental shootings, while others find that right-to-carry laws (including permitless carry) have no significant effect on violent crime or may even reduce it by deterring criminals.

Sheriff's offices will need to allocate resources and staff time to verify applicant eligibility and process permits. The administrative cost depends on application volume and the efficiency of the background-check process.

Applicants will bear the cost of the eight-hour safety course, which includes course fees charged by private instructors and the opportunity cost of the time required. The county sheriff's office will incur administrative costs to process applications and issue permits, which may not be covered if no fee is authorized.

Individuals seeking to carry a concealed handgun bear the time and financial costs of the required training. Private firearms instructors benefit from increased demand for safety courses. Local taxpayers may ultimately bear the administrative cost of the sheriff processing applications if the measure is unfunded.

Some individuals may choose not to carry a concealed handgun rather than spend the time and money to complete the 8-hour course. Private firearms instructors will likely expand course offerings to meet the new demand.

The county sheriff gains the regulatory authority to process applications, though the "shall issue" language limits their discretion. Firearms instructors gain a captive market of individuals legally required to complete their courses.

flags.quote: The sheriff shall issue a permit
flags.note: Requires the sheriff to issue permits without specifying any funding mechanism or allowable application fee to cover the administrative costs.
